notes:
Account background: DevPilot builds an IDE-integrated copilot used by internal dev teams and an enterprise plugin sold to ISVs. They need deterministic performance for interactive completion and streaming tokens, esp during peak developer hours (08:00–18:00 PT).

Summary of requirements: low single-token latency (~<40ms p50), sustained concurrency of 450 active devs during office hours, burst headroom to 900 concurrent sessions, strict model/version pinning for reproducibility, repo-aware reranking for multi-repo code search, and rolling canary rollouts to prevent regressions. Very cost-aware on non-peak hours.

Security: must support SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS-backed key management, audit logs stored 1 year, EU data residency for EU engineering org. Compliance: SOC2 required; ISO requested by one customer.

Quote from CTO (10/12 call): "We need predictable latency more than raw throughput — our developers will abandon the copilot if completions stutter. But we can't spend cloud money 24/7."

Why Redwood: liked the unified API + dedicated pools model. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching to reduce token costs without degrading latency. Keen on burst policies and automatic fallback to smaller model variants during spikes.

Commercial: target ARR mid six-figs, procurement tied to successful 2-week POC that reproduces dev-hour load. Legal has a couple of redlines on data residency and audit log export.

Notes taken by AE: prioritize demo of streaming p50 p90 numbers, show model-pinning UI, walk through canary rollback. Keep SE engaged for perf tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization).
